links.comparator_used: Base model with no governance prompt (generic prompt relying on built-in knowledge)
links.outcome: Under-triage (failure to escalate to the top acuity tier) in subtle or atypical emergencies
links.effect: Across 76 stems, under-triage fell from 13.2% (95% CI 7.3 to 22.6) to 3.9% (1.4 to 11.0); McNemar 7 to 0, p = 0.016; RR 0.30; NNT 11. Across eight models, 19 stems favoured governance and 5 favoured control (sign test p = 0.007). Named-guideline citation rose from 65.6% to 96.9%. MedQA was unchanged at 95.8% in both arms.
links.tradeoff: Moved some ROUTINE non-emergency stems to same-day URGENT (17 added vs 2 removed, p < 0.001). HealthBench fell 3.6 points on a single seed. Residual failures stayed concentrated in a few conditions, and some model/elicitation cells were neutral or reversed.
links.quote: Across 76 subtle or atypical emergencies, each adjudicated by a blinded, LLM-simulated three-physician panel and each mapped to a published guideline that names its cannot-miss diagnosis, the base model failed to escalate 13.2% (95% CI 7.3 to 22.6) to the top acuity tier; the governance prompt cut this to 3.9% (1.4 to 11.0; paired exact McNemar 7 to 0, p = 0.016; relative risk 0.30; number needed to treat 11).

links.comparator_used: Forced immediate single-shot disposition (direct answer) vs reasoning-permitted elicitation on the same models
links.outcome: Baseline under-triage hazard by elicitation mode
links.effect: Forcing an immediate single-shot disposition raised baseline hazard by roughly ten percentage points in two of four Claude models.
links.quote: Elicitation mattered: forcing an immediate single-shot disposition raised baseline hazard by roughly ten percentage points in two of four Claude models, and the governance increment in the Claude family was largest under that elicitation.

design_hint: prompt guardrails for emergency triage escalation
